title: Coherent modules on a scheme: kernels, cokernels, extensions and finite direct sums are coherent
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] (more generally any ringed space) and let $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with its kernels (sectionwise) and cokernels (sheafified sectionwise quotients). No Noetherian hypothesis is made. (1) If $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent], then $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ are coherent. (2) If $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F_2\to\mathcal F_3\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and two of $\mathcal F_1,\mathcal F_2,\mathcal F_3$ are coherent, so is the third. (3) In particular, for coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F_1,\dots,\mathcal F_r$ ($r\ge0$) the direct sum $\mathcal F_1\oplus\dots\oplus\mathcal F_r$ is coherent (for $r=0$ the zero module), and so is every $\mathcal O_X$-module isomorphic to a coherent one.

proof.text: Finite type transports along isomorphisms by transporting local generating sections through the restricted isomorphism. The kernel condition transports via kernelCompMono. The zero sheaf has the empty global generating tuple; relations into its restriction are kernels of zero maps and thus finite free sheaves, whose basis is a finite global generating tuple. These steps are implemented as proved private helpers.
For f:F to G between coherent modules, its kernel is finite type by the finite type kernel lemma, and then coherent as a finite type submodule of F.
The cokernel is finite type as an epimorphic image of G. Its relation kernels are finite type by lem-weil-pbc-coherent-cokernel-relations. These are exactly the two fields of IsCoherent.

In a short exact sequence with coherent end terms, the middle term is finite type by finiteType_image_extension and its relation kernels are finite type by lem-weil-pbc-coherent-extension-relations. If the first and middle terms are coherent, identify the last with the cokernel of the first map; if the middle and last are coherent, identify the first with the kernel of the last map. Transport coherence along the universal-property isomorphisms.

Induct on r. The empty biproduct is zero by the biproduct universal property. For Fin (r+1), the inclusions from the tail biproduct and the projection onto index zero form a split short exact sequence. Construct its retraction and section using the biproduct universal properties and check the splitting identity on each projection using Fin.cases. Apply the extension conclusion to the coherent tail and the coherent first summand. Isomorphism invariance and zero coherence were established directly in the first step.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 01BY's proof. Checked pqf-def-coherent: it is the Stacks 01BV notion (finite type, plus finite type kernels of all local maps from finite free modules), stated for schemes, so no Noetherian hypothesis is needed and the item's statement matches it; the proof is written for schemes (opens of a scheme are schemes, needed for lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover) and holds verbatim on ringed spaces. Seven steps: preliminaries (iso invariance, zero module, locality of finite type, restriction preserves exactness via lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-module-exactness-local-lifting); kernel via 01BY (1)-(2); cokernel finite type and the image sequence; cokernel coherent by the snake lemma; two-out-of-three (two cases from kernels/cokernels, the extension case by the snake lemma); direct sums by induction. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-image-extension (Stacks 01B7, unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-coherent-finite-type-sub-kernel (Stacks 01BY (1), (2), unsplit), lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-abelian (Stacks 010H, Mathlib leaf SnakeInput.snake_lemma; the existing lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules is for modules over a ring only). stmt_deps kept.
